Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Manoj Bajaj,J.
Vimlesh Singraur-Appellant has filed this appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 to challenge the order dated 3.6.2024 passed by Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Fathepur, whereby his application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail, during the pendency of trial in Case Crime No. 63 of 2024, under Sections 376, 342,
313, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)V Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act, 1989, Police Station Kishanpur, District Fatehpur has been rejected.

Learned counsel for appellant has argued that the allegations by prosecutrix are highly improbable,
who allegedly had left her parental house to reach the matrimonial home alongwith jewellery and cash when she was asked by the appellant to accompany him as the mother of the prosecutrix was not well.

Learned counsel submits that as per the allegations, the accused-appellant took her to a one room accommodation where she stayed for a period of more than two months and was subjected to rape and even four months pregnancy at the time of leaving the house was aborted by Vimlesh Singraur vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: Learned counsel submits that the place where the prosecutrix resided is not an isolated place and the other tenants were also residing there, who during investigation got their statement recorded that the couple resided as husband and wife.

Learned counsel submits that the complainant left her house on 1.6.2023, whereas the F.I.R. has been lodged after a long delay and a missing report by father of the prosecutrix lodged on 2.6.2023 clearly says that she had left the house without informing any family member.

Learned counsel submits that the stand of the complainant that she left her house to accompany her husband is contradictory to the version of her father and the allegations of abortion or rape are not supported by any medical evidence.
Learned counsel for appellant submits that Special Court, Fatehpur has not carefully examined the facts and circumstances of the case while rejecting his bail application.
He prays that impugned order dated 3.6.2024 be set aside and the appellant be released on regular bail.
Despite service, no one has appeared on behalf of complainant-respondent no.2.
The prayer is opposed by learned A.G.A., who has argued that complainant specifically named the appellant and on the basis of her statement, the charge sheet has been filed.
Learned A.G.A. fairly states that the site plan revealing the alleged place of confinement also shows the presence of other tenants and their statement during investigation was also recorded.

Learned A.G.A. submits that trial court has considered the material on record carefully while rejecting the bail application filed by the appellant, and the order dated 3.6.2024 is based upon correct appreciation of material,
therefore, the said order does not call for any interference in exercise of appellate jurisdiction.

After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and considering their submissions, this Court is of the considered opinion that as the investigation in the case is complete, therefore, further detention of the appellant behind the bars may not be necessary for any useful purpose, who is confined in judicial custody after his arrest on 31.3.2024.
The material witnesses in the case are either the complainant or the police officials and at present, there does not seem to be any possibility of their being won over.

Further, the conclusion of trial is likely to consume considerable time and a perusal of the impugned order dated 3.6.2024 would show that Special Court, Fatehpur has not properly appreciated the facts and circumstances of the case while refusing to exercise the discretion in favour of the accused
, therefore, the impugned order dated 3.6.2024 is not sustainable, as it is a fit case for extending the concession of regular bail to the appellant.

Resultantly, without meaning any expression of opinion on the merits of the case, the impugned order dated 3.6.2024 is set aside, the bail application filed by the appellant under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is hereby accepted, and it is ordered that the appellant?Vimlesh Singraur be released on regular bail in the above case crime subject to his furnishing the requisite bail bonds and surety bonds to the satisfaction of the trial court.
The appeal is allowed.
